why: The C4 replacement made the model avoid cutting between a noun (or its specifier) and a required postnominal modifier, so cuts that used to occur there were moved elsewhere; that shift helps some mid-length pieces but increases harmful splits in very-short bins (e.g. subject–verb breaks or internal compound-noun splits), producing a small net negative. The by_bin pattern (hurt at ≤3 and ≤5, help at ≤7/≤10) and the tails (many examples where a safe noun-modifier cut was replaced by a subject‑verb or compound split) support this.
lesson: Do not blanket-forbid cuts after nouns — preventing noun+modifier splits can simply move cuts into very short phrases and create worse subject–verb or compound-noun splits, so later revisions should avoid that wholesale prohibition.
